$comment: The ingestion write contract, shared by every writer.
`lib/ingest/upsert-sql.ts` (the API) and `scripts/ingest.py` (the bulk CLI)
both read this file. Neither may hold its own copy of the column list or the
precedence rule — those rules decide what overwrites production data, so two
implementations would be two chances to get it wrong, and only one of them
would be the one under test.
A column present in the concordance but absent here is SILENTLY DROPPED on
the way to the database, not rejected. conformance.test.ts asserts the two
stay in step; six columns had already gone missing that way.
Templates use {incoming}, {existing} and {mode} placeholders. {incoming} and
{existing} are SQL aliases — EXCLUDED / filings inside an ON CONFLICT clause,
or CTE aliases elsewhere. {mode} is the placeholder bound to
'skip' | 'overwrite'.
Two distinct rules, and the distinction matters:
e-file over e-file is a RESUBMISSION, not a conflict — the later
SUB_DATE wins automatically and the operator is never asked;
everything else is a cross-source conflict, governed by the operator's
skip/overwrite choice for that load.
A winning row uses COALESCE(incoming, existing) per column, so a load may
add information but can never blank a populated value.
precedence.incoming_wins:
(
    ({both_efile}
       AND {incoming}.submission_date IS NOT NULL
       AND ({existing}.submission_date IS NULL
            OR {incoming}.submission_date >= {existing}.submission_date))
    OR
    (NOT ({both_efile}) AND {mode} = 'overwrite')
  )
precedence.audit_action:
CASE
    WHEN NOT {incoming_wins} THEN 'skipped'
    WHEN {both_efile} THEN 'superseded'
    ELSE 'overwritten'
  END
